title: Telling Time Worksheets to 5 Minutes
intro: Use a clock with movable hands to teach time to the nearest five minutes.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Count by fives around the clock with your student. Then point out which hour the short hand has passed, especially when it is close to the next hour.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

4:20: the long hand points to 4. Count 5, 10, 15, 20. The short hand is just past 4, so the time is 4:20.

Ask your student

At 7:55, has the hour hand reached 8 yet?

If your student needs help

If the student reads the face number as minutes, count the five-minute intervals from 12 together.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set contains six distinct times. Minutes range from :00 through :55 in five-minute steps, including hours and half hours when selected. The clock drawings show twelve face numbers and two hands. Sets do not guarantee every minute value.

This activity covers reading an analog clock and recording a digital time. A clock face alone cannot determine AM or PM. Choosing AM or PM from a daily-life context, drawing hands, and calculating elapsed time are not assessed here.
